narrative_arc: From noisy EEG graph construction, through a two-stage Transformer plus LLM edge-refinement method, to TUSZ detection performance and physiological interpretability.

slides.primary_proposition: LLM as Clinical Graph Structure Refiner uses language-model reasoning to improve EEG seizure diagnosis.
must_cover_subset: Exact paper title: LLM as Clinical Graph Structure Refiner: Enhancing Representation Learning in EEG Seizure Diagnosis
Authors: Lincan Li, Zheng Chen, Yushun Dong
Core claim: LLM refinement removes redundant EEG graph edges and improves representation quality

slides.primary_proposition: Noisy, variable EEG signals make both predefined and learned channel graphs prone to spurious connections.
must_cover_subset: EEG seizure events vary in duration, frequency, and spatial manifestation across patients
Correlation, distance, KNN, attention, and generative graph methods can retain redundant or erroneous edges
Misleading connectivity degrades GNN representation learning, detection, and interpretability

slides.primary_proposition: The proposed pipeline first predicts candidate edges, then asks an LLM to validate each connection before diagnosis.
must_cover_subset: Stage 1: Transformer channel embeddings plus an MLP produce edge probabilities and a thresholded initial graph
Stage 2: an LLM receives node-pair evidence and returns yes/no for each candidate edge
The refined graph feeds a GraphS4mer representation model for seizure prediction and explanation

slides.primary_proposition: Each edge decision combines semantic channel descriptions with twelve statistical EEG features.
must_cover_subset: Text features include channel label, anatomical region, signal observations, and temporal trend
Statistics include mean, standard deviation, dominant frequency, min, max, median, quartiles, skewness, kurtosis, energy, and zero crossings
The prompt asks whether a physiologically meaningful functional connection exists between the node pair

slides.primary_proposition: The benchmark isolates graph quality by holding the GraphS4mer backbone and TUSZ evaluation protocol fixed.
must_cover_subset: TUSZ v1.5.2 contains 5,612 EEG recordings and 3,050 seizure annotations
Nineteen channels use the standard 10–20 montage
Ten LLM refiners are compared with five non-LLM graph constructors using F1, accuracy, and recall

slides.primary_proposition: LLM-refined graphs consistently outperform conventional graph construction on seizure detection.
must_cover_subset: Best conventional result: Generative Graph Learner, F1 0.7351, accuracy 0.9039, recall 0.7625
GPT-5 plus Transformer graph reaches F1 0.7907, accuracy 0.9315, recall 0.8058
GPT-5-mini reaches F1 0.7859; GPT-4.1 reaches 0.7792

slides.primary_proposition: Graph reasoning becomes sparser and more consistent as the structural judge grows stronger.
must_cover_subset: Mistral 7B: graph sparsity 0.4213 and JSD 0.0576
GPT-4o: sparsity 0.3826 and JSD 0.0314
GPT-5: sparsity 0.3741 and the lowest JSD, 0.0265

slides.primary_proposition: Node importance tracks a clinically plausible seizure spread from frontal toward temporal regions.
must_cover_subset: Across t+1 to t+6, activation moves from Fp1/Fp2/F3/F4 toward T3/T4
GPT-family refiners show more stable and spatially focused activations than Mistral and Llama
GPT-5 produces the most coherent and biologically plausible feature pattern

slides.primary_proposition: Spatiotemporal graph visualizations show that stronger LLMs preserve seizure propagation with fewer redundant links.
must_cover_subset: The case study follows frontal, temporal, central, and parietal–occipital propagation over four windows
GPT-5 and GPT-4o produce sparse, spatially coherent connectivity
Gemini 2.5-Pro adds some redundant inter-region links; Llama 3.1-70B is denser and noisier

slides.primary_proposition: LLMs can act as clinically informed graph refiners, improving accuracy and interpretability without changing the downstream backbone.
must_cover_subset: The contribution is edge validation, not replacement of EEG signal modeling
Results support language-driven reasoning as a mechanism for pruning task-irrelevant connectivity
Future work targets domain-adaptive prompting, multimodal integration, robustness, and broader biomedical graphs
